title: Video Capture - Turn Table
content: **List of Contents** Turn Table Video Capture Record Turn Table Video Edit Turn Table Video Save Turn Table Video **Turn Table Video Capture** \- Record the 3D Garment in CLO to share with others for efficient communication. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Turn Table.** ** Record Turn Table Video** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VRwsDh8A4T4 \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Turn Table.** \- The Turn Table Video Capture window will appear on the bottom of the window. \- Modify the options under the Video Size, Options, and the Video Codec sections. \- After adjusting the options as needed, select the **Record button.** \- When the recording is done, the preview window will appear. **Edit Turn Table Video** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2LDgtx_b_0 \- Edit the recording in the preview window. \- Split the video by right-clicking and selecting the **Split** option on the timeline bar. \- Then, select the timeline to be deleted and right click and select the **Delete** option. **Save Turn Table Video** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2_HPWu5ez9g \- Select the **Save** button to save the edited recording. \- Assign the saving path and the file name and click **Save.** \- The recording will be saved. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to capture, edit, and save Turn Table videos of 3D garments in CLO for effective sharing and communication.

title: Animation Import
content: **Objective** Import Animation cache data created in the third-party 3D solutions. **※ Note:** Refer to the links below for FBX/ Alembic file import:. * [3D File (FBX) Import/Export ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000526908-3D%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-FBX-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EB%82%B4%EB%B3%B4%EB%82%B4%EA%B8%B0) * [3D File (Alembic) Import/Export](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000499067-3D%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-Alembic-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EB%82%B4%EB%B3%B4%EB%82%B4%EA%B8%B0) ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ * **Maya Cache(.mc) ** * **Maya Cache(.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache(Standard) ** * **MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ * **Maya Cache(.mc) ** * **Maya Cache(.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache(Standard) ** * **MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max)** → The File Explorer or Find window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click**OK**. → An option window appears with settings that apply to the file format selected. 3. Set the following individual settings. **Object** | **Select All Avatars** | Apply the cache data to all objects in the 3D environment. Cache data can be applied to individual objects from the submenu. ---|---|--- **FPS** | Set the frame rate of the cache data. **※ Note:** This menu only appears when importing Point Cache (PC2) files. **Scale** | Set the scale of the cache data. **Axis Conversion** | Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. **Garment Position** | **Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position** | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). **Transition Animation** | A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motion’s first pose in stages, and is created when the avatar’s current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. 4. Click **OK**. → The cache data is imported according to the selected settings.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing animation cache data from third-party 3D solutions such as Maya and Alembic, ensuring seamless integration into your projects.

title: Change Pose by Collada's Joint Information
content: **Objective** **※ Note:** Only available for file formats with avatar joint information. In this case, COLLADA is being used. As avatar's joints move as the pose changes, it is able to change avatar pose while keeping the stimulation stably even if there is a large difference between the starting and the end poses. However if the avatar is formatted via DAZ Studio, some composition form information may be lost during the process. Therefore there is a need to load the posed avatar's OBJ file and adjust garments after changing the pose. (The avatar's OBJ file only saves the composition form information, there is no danger of losses in the loading process.) ** Operation** 1. Export a T-pose avatar which can be easily draped and an avatar with the final pose in COLLADA files. To find out export methods from DAZ Studio and Poser in details, check [3D File (COLLADA) Import](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000531948) for the reference. 2. After exporting the COLLADA files, export the avatar poses in OBJ files. 3. Load a posed COLLADA file from the previously saved avatars in CLO 3D/MD. 4. Click File ▶ Save ▶ **Pose** to save current avatar as POS file. After dressing T-pose avatar, this file is going to be used when changing current pose. 5. Click File ▶ Open ▶ **Avatar** to open the previously saved T-pose COLLADA file. Dress the avatar with desired garments. 6. Now Click File ▶ Open ▶ **Pose** to open the previously saved POS file. The avatar slowly changes poses. It may take a while depending on the complexity of the garments. 7. After the pose changes, load an OBJ file without any loss and adjust garments. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** to open the previously saved final pose OBJ file. Highly positive to observe garments being under the avatar's surface. 8. While simulation is being activated, drag out the parts that are gone under the avatar's surface by using left mouse button. To find more details in **Select/Move** tool, check [Move Garment](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000304968) for the reference.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adjusting avatar poses in CLO 3D/MD using COLLADA and OBJ file formats to ensure accurate garment fitting and simulation.

title: Physical Property Detail Setting
content: Adjust each item of the detailed settings to express Physical Properties not included in Presets. Each property mutually affects one another and a Garment's physical property is expressed by combination of all detailed property values. **※ Note:** * The property details are adjustable with the scroll bar or by entering in actual measurement values. ** ** * **Scroll Bar [0~99]** : This is better input method when the constant value is far too enormous. To reduce this inconvenience, the most commonly used Physical Property is split into 99 stages. * **Constant Value [0~1000000000]** This is better input method when setting far more accurate Physical Properties than the scroll bar method above.
content_description: "Customize and fine-tune each physical property of your garment through adjustable settings to achieve precise and unique results beyond preset options."

title: Scale OBJ Trims
content: **List of Contents** Transform OBJ Trims Scale OBJ Dimension **Transform OBJ Trims YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dO8YCXIusFg **\- Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. \- Select the imported OBJ file loaded as trim and select the**Scale button** hovering over the trim. \- Select the OBJ file loaded as trim and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Scale OBJ Dimension** * **Via the Scale Gizmo YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YKI7gz-pbgM ** \- Load an OBJ file as a trim. \- Click on the OBJ and select the **Scale button** on the right top corner. \- The **Scale Gizmo** is formed with three axes and one square. \- Select the Scale button again to complete the transformation. * **Axis** \- Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. \- Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. \- Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. * **Square** \- Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ, maintaining its x,y,z dimensional ratio. * **Via the Property Editor YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AOw5OCKnmVg ** \- Select the OBJ trim to be scaled. \- The selected OBJ’s properties appear in the Property Editor. \- Find and adjust properties under the Scale (Local) menu as needed. * **Scale (Local)** \- X： Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. \- Y： Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. \- Z： Type in the value to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. \- **Lock Aspect Ratio** : Transform the OBJ file while maintaining its dimensional ratio. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for transforming and scaling OBJ trim files using various methods, including video tutorials and detailed instructions.

title: Order of Use of the Modular Configurator Window
content: Follow the order of use of the Modualr Configurator window in order to construct and use an user data. To create a configuration file for the Modular Configurator, please follow the steps below: Open the Modular Configurator window ▶ Add an User folder by pressing (**+**) icon ▶ Press the **Edit** icon to switch to the Editor Mode ▶ If needed, add groups by pressing **Add Group** icon ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zmdr) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Designate the Modular file (.zblc) to either be displayed or hidden for each group ▶ Click **Save** button to save the structure file in the same folder as the Block ▶ Press **Exit** button when editing is done
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for constructing and managing user data using the Modular Configurator window.

title: General Process of Using Modular Mode
content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template ▶ Add Patterns or Garments ▶ Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes ▶ Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes ▶ Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)
content_description: Create and manage your own Pattern database by following the Modular Mode procedures for seamless design and construction.

title: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### **Objective** Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. ** Location** Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular Configurator** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular Configurator** → Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. → Folders appear in order. 3. Select a desired Garment category folder. → Modular Structure file is displayed. 4. Select a desired Modular Structure file. → All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 5. Select a desired Block. → The Blocks are replaced accordingly. 6. Modify the design as desired and complete the 3D Garment.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of selecting and combining Blocks in the Modular Configurator to create customized 3D garments.

title: Edit Measurement
content: ### **Objective** Edit avatar measurements. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab** ### **Operation ** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab**** ** → The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. 2. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. **Name** | Rename the measurement. | **Basic Length** | Check the measurement's basic length. ---|---|---|--- **Measurement Type** | Change the measurement type. | **Surface Length** | Check the surface length of the measurement. **Measurement Information** | Check the measurement's information. | **Show** | Show or hide the selected measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a user-friendly interface for editing and managing avatar measurements within the Avatar Editor.

title: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: **Objective** Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. **※ Note:** For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that [Skin Offset](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002227387) is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. **Location** Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Simulation Thickness property for garments to optimize collision limits and achieve smooth fabric simulations in design software.

title: Delete All Overlapping Points
content: **Objective** Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When importing *.dxf files created in other CAD programs or cutting Patterns in CLO, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by CLO. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** → All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for deleting overlapping points in patterns and internal shapes within CLO, ensuring smooth editing and movement of imported DXF files.
